previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with dizziness and hypotension, initially attributed to recent diarrhea and low baseline blood pressure. He reported right knee pain, and examination revealed a swollen, tender knee. Arthrocentesis showed hemarthrosis with no infection. Blood cultures grew Staphylococcus epidermidis, suggesting a dialysis line infection. He was started on vancomycin, and after two negative cultures, underwent a tunneled dialysis line exchange over wire. The old catheter tip culture confirmed gram-positive cocci. His knee pain improved with fluid removal and analgesia, and he had no signs of endocarditis on echocardiogram. He completed scheduled dialysis, remained afebrile, and was discharged to extended care with a two-week course of vancomycin during dialysis and instructions to monitor the line site and weight.

to place the tunneled dialysis line.  Patent left subclavian vein was accessed
with micropuncture needle under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance.  A
micropuncture wire was passed through and the needle was exchanged for a
micropuncture sheath.  A ___ was attempted to pass into the superior vena
cava, but due to the tortuosity of the vessel it was unable to pass the wire
into the SVC.  A 4 ___ C2 glide catheter was advanced over super stiff
glide after the tract was dilated with a 6 ___ dilator.  The catheter was
used to direct the wire into the IVC.  The catheter was then extended into the
IVC and the Glidewire was exchanged for an Amplatz.  Now, attention was
directed towards the left chest wall.  After appropriate measurements were
taken, tunnel was created with a tunneling device and appropriate numbing with
lidocaine and lidocaine with epinephrine.  Serial dilation of the tract was
performed with 12 and 14 ___ dilators.  A peel-away sheath was placed over
the Amplatz wire.  The inner dilator was removed and the catheter was fed into
the peel-away sheath over the Amplatz wire.  Once the catheter was in place,
the sheath was peeled away and Amplatz wire was removed.  The venotomy site
was closed with ___ Vicryl and the catheter was secured to the skin with 0
silk sutures.  Secured dressings were applied.

The attention was now directed to the left groin with a temporary hemodialysis
line was removed and hemostasis was achieved by manual compression for 5
minutes.

Sterile dressings were applied.  The patient had pain in his right leg, which
was unrelated to the procedure and had been complaining of pain throughout the
procedure.  There were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Successful uncomplicated placement of left subclavian 14.5 ___ 31 cm
tip-to-cuff tunneled hemodialysis line.  The tip is in the right atrium.  The
line is ready to use.

2.  Successful uncomplicated removal of 12 ___ temporary hemodialysis line
with a VIP port.
